documents: Hossain, Kamei & Araoka 2022, Geological Journal 57:3431-3446 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: Because no systematic petrographic and geochemical studies (combined major oxides, trace elements and REEs) have been made about island sediments in the Bay of Bengal

sequences.source_document: Hossain, Kamei & Araoka 2022, Geological Journal (published PDF)

steps.action: Pose the aim of determining the compositional maturity, provenance and source-rock weathering of Sonadia Island shoreline sediments, citing a gap in combined petrographic and geochemical work.
steps.quote: to investigate their compositional maturity, provenance and source-rock weathering

steps.action: Collect twenty shoreline sediment samples along Sonadia Island, then air-dry, grind and oven-dry them.
steps.quote: Twenty sediment samples were collected along the shoreline of Sonadia Island.

steps.action: Point-count thin sections (Gazzi-Dickinson, about 600 points per sample) for QFL modes and grain size, and classify the sands as quartz-rich sublitharenite.
steps.quote: The samples are characterized by high quartz (74–83%) and low feldspar (7–12%)

steps.action: Identify the main minerals of selected samples by SEM-EDS.
steps.quote: quartz, plagioclase feldspar, K-feldspar, ilmenite, magnetite, titanite and zircon are the most common minerals

steps.action: Measure major oxides and trace elements by XRF on glass beads, REE by LA-ICP-MS on 13 samples, and LOI by ignition.
steps.quote: SiO2 exhibits the highest abundances of 88.19–94.06 wt% (average 91.43 wt%)

steps.action: Check XRF reliability by replicate analysis of ten GSJ standard rocks at run time (Methods).
steps.quote: The reliability of major-oxide and trace-element concentrations was assessed by replicate analysis of ten Geological Survey of Japan standard rocks at run time.

steps.action: Correlate oxides, trace elements and REE against Al2O3 and total REE (trend lines fitted by eye) and assign the elements to host minerals: quartz, phyllosilicates, feldspar, heavy minerals.
steps.quote: indicating that silica is mainly controlled by the quartz content rather than aluminosilicates

steps.action: Plot the QFL modes on the Dickinson et al. (1983) ternary diagram, where all samples fall in the quartzose recycled orogen field, close to Cox's Bazar sand and Bengal Fan sands.
steps.quote: the Sonadia Island sands fall entirely within the quartzose recycled orogen field

steps.action: Normalize the compositions to average UCC and read the depletion in Na, Ca, Mg, Sr and Sc as plagioclase destruction during fluvial transport, with a felsic, UCC-like source.
steps.quote: There is marked depletion of Na, Ca, Mg, Sr and Sc relative to UCC, indicating destruction of plagioclase during fluvial transport.

steps.action: Compute ICV and the SiO2/Al2O3, Al2O3/Na2O and K2O/Na2O ratios to estimate compositional and textural maturity against published thresholds.
steps.quote: suggesting a low to moderate degree of compositional maturity

steps.action: Take the expected signatures of mafic, intermediate, felsic and quartzose recycled sources from published discrimination schemes and ratio thresholds (Roser & Korsch, Hayashi et al., McLennan et al., Floyd & Leveridge).
steps.quote: to distinguish mafic (P1), intermediate (P2), felsic (P3) and quartzose recycled (P4) provenances

steps.action: Compare the samples with the F1-F2 discriminant diagram, the K2O-Rb plot and the Al2O3/TiO2, TiO2/Zr, Th/Sc and Zr/Sc ratios; all fall in the quartzose recycled or felsic fields.
steps.quote: the Sonadia Island sediments entirely lie in the lowermost part of the P4 field, suggesting a quartzose recycled provenance

steps.action: Check each provenance plot against the authors' earlier Cox's Bazar beach sand dataset, which plots close to the present samples.
steps.quote: The plot is close to the compositional field of Cox's Bazar beach sand (Hossain et al., 2018), further confirming a quartzose recycled provenance.

steps.action: Reject a mafic or ultramafic source because Cr and Ni are low, Cr/V is low, Y/Ni is high and Th/U is UCC-like.
steps.quote: The shoreline samples contain low levels of Cr (3.0–41.7 ppm) and Ni (5.4–12.8 ppm), again indicating a felsic source composition.

steps.action: Compare the chondrite-normalized REE patterns, Eu anomaly, LaN/YbN, GdN/YbN and LREE/HREE ratios with felsic and mafic expectations and with UCC and PAAS.
steps.quote: The Sonadia Island samples display a fractionated chondrite-normalized REE pattern with high LaN/YbN ratios

steps.action: Compare the REE patterns with published Himalayan source rocks and sediments (Yarlung Zangbo suture sedimentary rocks, Nepal boulders, Rewalsar lake sediments).
steps.quote: the REE distribution patterns of the shoreline sediments are nearly identical to those of Himalaya–Tibetan Plateau sediments and rocks

steps.action: Refine the reading by attributing element enrichments in fine fractions and in sample S-1 to hydrodynamic sorting and heavy-mineral concentration at the coast.
steps.quote: their abundances are likely connected to the hydrodynamic conditions of the coast

steps.action: Compute CIA (with an apatite correction to CaO), CIW, PIA and a K-corrected CIA from the A-CN-K diagram to estimate source-area weathering intensity.
steps.quote: The CIA values in the shoreline sediments are 63.4–69.3 (average 66.4, Table 2), reflecting low to moderate chemical weathering.

steps.action: Cross-check the weathering intensity with the independent Rb/Sr and K2O/Rb ratio proxies.
steps.quote: again indicating moderate chemical weathering in the source area

steps.action: Keep the claim of a felsic, UCC-like, quartzose recycled Himalaya-Tibetan source that had undergone moderate weathering.
steps.quote: The overall geochemical characteristics and patterns of the Sonadia Island sediments are consistent with those of rocks in the Himalaya–Tibetan orogen

tree.answer: Composition of shoreline sediments of Sonadia Island
No; source and weathering are inferred from sediment traces
Implicit source categories: mafic, intermediate, felsic, quartzose recycled
Published discrimination fields and ratio thresholds separate the source categories
Conditions found; modern sediments sampled once
Consistent across many proxies and with the Cox's Bazar dataset
Felsic UCC-like recycled Himalayan source; moderate weathering

end.claim: The Sonadia Island shoreline sediments derive from felsic, UCC-like, quartzose recycled detritus of the Himalaya-Tibetan orogen whose source rocks underwent moderate chemical weathering.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing the samples' compositions and ratios with published provenance discrimination fields and thresholds is what yields the felsic, recycled-source claim.

gates.evidence: Sampling and analysis were set by a gap in the literature, not by a hypothesis (p. 3433). The discrimination diagrams could in principle have placed the samples in mafic or intermediate fields (pp. 3440-3442), but no test is framed with failure criteria, and the Figure 3 trend lines are fitted by eye. Nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: X-ray fluorescence spectrometry (Rigaku RIX 2000) on fused glass beads
Laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry for REE
Scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive spectrometry
Discriminant function analysis (Roser & Korsch 1988 diagram) and correlation coefficients

novelty_claims.quote: no systematic petrographic and geochemical studies (combined major oxides, trace elements and REEs) have been made about island sediments in the Bay of Bengal, Bangladesh

limits: Sub-claims and their statuses: the compositional maturity reading (low to moderate) and the weathering intensity (moderate) are estimate_with_resolution, but no analytical uncertainties are given; the hydrodynamic-sorting attribution is best_explanation. Correlations are not tested for significance, and the Figure 3 trend lines are fitted by eye (p. 3440). REE were measured on only 13 of the 20 samples (Table 3). Inference: Th by XRF (average 11.5 ppm, Table 2) and Th by LA-ICP-MS (average 4.83 ppm, Table 3) differ by more than a factor of two, and the paper does not discuss this. There are internal inconsistencies: the abstract gives CIA 65-69 while Table 2 gives 63.4-69.3; Al2O3/TiO2 is 15-38 in the abstract and 16-38 in the text; the ICV average is printed as '90'. The comparison with Himalayan sources is qualitative, and Indo-Burman/Chittagong-Tripura versus Himalayan contributions are not separated by a decisive test. The GSJ standard results are not reported. The peer-review history is only linked (p. 3445), not supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

disagreements.target: Hoque et al. (2021): Sonadia Island is far from present-day delta building
disagreements.support: The authors state, without new data, that tidal circulation nonetheless delivers large sediment volumes to the studied shoreline.
disagreements.quote: however, the investigated shoreline near Sonadia Island (Figure 1) receives large amounts of sediments from the highland region through tidal current/circulation processes

alternatives_considered.chosen: CaO corrected for Ca in apatite
Measured CIA alongside a K-corrected CIA from the A-CN-K diagram

v_checks.quote: The reliability of major-oxide and trace-element concentrations was assessed by replicate analysis of ten Geological Survey of Japan standard rocks at run time.
Rare-earth element profiles, discrimination diagrams and various elemental ratios are all consistent with the derivation of the sediment from a felsic igneous source area.
The plot is close to the compositional field of Cox's Bazar beach sand (Hossain et al., 2018), further confirming a quartzose recycled provenance.
again indicating moderate chemical weathering in the source area
